local_probe.evidence: The probe fixed Date at zero, exposed no process/fetch/require globals, stopped an infinite loop, resolved a relative in-memory module, and ran 1,000 fresh contexts.

candidates.reason: It is the only candidate that combines a memory-safe engine, no built-in host authority, deterministic clock control, in-memory modules, engine-level termination, and source-level portability across every Runx release target.

decision.worker_design: A runtime session lazily reuses a bounded pool of up to four supervised runx-js-worker processes. Each process executes one invocation at a time, creates a fresh Boa context per invocation, loads only a validated in-memory relative module bundle, and communicates over a versioned length-delimited JSON protocol.
rationale: The engine contributes no Node, browser, filesystem, network, process, environment, credential, clock, or randomness host surface.
Pure Rust source passed checks for all five Runx release targets without introducing a C cross-toolchain into releases.
The measured fresh-context cost is 118 microseconds, leaving ample margin versus the current process-per-step lane.
Engine loop limits, fixed clock support, and embedded module loading are available without custom native bindings.
A separate process remains mandatory because an in-process language engine is not the aggregate memory, crash, or wall-time security boundary.
decision.release_gate: Do not switch the production javascript lane until the worker passes the hostile-module suite and hard memory/wall/process isolation checks on every release target, and the measured runtime budgets do not regress beyond the approved baseline.

rejected_alternatives.reason: Stronger structural no-import isolation does not offset the Wasmtime dependency, compilation layer, artifact size, and measured memory overhead for this bounded worker.
Superior microbenchmark speed does not offset native C-engine release complexity and incomplete deterministic/all-target evidence.
